title: Looking back: the depths
hookLine: the immeasurables, mindfulness, emptiness, koans, the elders, the diamond vehicle
tomorrow: The first mountain, from the top

cards: From a boat, the sea is a flat blue surface. Put on a mask and lower your face into the water, and there's a whole world down there: a reef, colors, a turtle drifting past as if it had all day.
The flat blue was never the whole story. The fifth camp was that moment. The stories, the practices and the book were the surface; the depths put your face in the water.

teach.b: First, the four immeasurables, four rooms to live in: metta, karuna, mudita and upekkha.
Loving-kindness, compassion, gladness at others' joy, and equanimity, each, as later teachers put it, with a near enemy that looks like it: pity for compassion, indifference for equanimity.

Then the Satipatthana, the direct path: the body, feelings, the mind, and the patterns of experience, watched ardently, aware and mindful. The second arrow you don't have to shoot. Knowing without fixing.
Seven years, or seven days. Then the Heart Sutra.
Form is emptiness, and emptiness is not nothing. No eye, no ear. Nothing to attain, and so, without fear.
Gate, gate. Then the koans, which you weren't supposed to solve. Mu.
Wash your bowl. The flag and the wind. Every day is a good day.
The sound of one hand. Then two electives, side by side, never ranked.
The way of the elders: three baskets, forest monks, rules as a shelter, calm and insight, rising and falling, entering the stream, Buddhaghosa's path of virtue, calm and wisdom.

teach.h: THE ELDERS AND THE DIAMOND VEHICLE.
teach.b: And the diamond vehicle: the six syllables, wheels and flags, the four thoughts, the teacher, tonglen, the slogans, bodhicitta, Tara, the sand swept into the river, the bardo.
Each of these could fill a lifetime, and for some people it does. You've had a first look. The Buddha said the teaching he found was deep and hard to see; a year in, that line holds a little more.
And this week's lines: when you're ready, many doors, come and see, the stories stay, you practice now, the verses stay.

how: Buddhists often spend years or a lifetime with one of these depths: the brahmaviharas, satipatthana practice, the Heart Sutra, koan study, or the Theravada and Tibetan paths, usually with a teacher and a community.

o: proof you've mastered the advanced teachings
a first glance into rooms that take a lifetime
a final exam on the year's hardest ideas

games.q: match each depth from the fifth camp.

s: the fifth camp ranked the elders above the diamond vehicle
the two electives were taught side by side, never ranked.
each immeasurable has a near enemy that looks like it
pity passes for compassion; indifference passes for equanimity.
the Buddha called his teaching deep and hard to see
the depths are a first look, not the whole of it.

games.q: the bell ends your two-minute sit. you have more time today, and the outline suggested twenty minutes. what does the path invite?
o: stop: two minutes is the rule.
keep sitting if you can; two minutes is still a whole sit.
start over with a new technique.
games.why: the longer sit is an invitation, not a test. there's more, whenever you're ready for it.

practice: If you have the time, sit longer today, up to twenty minutes: when the two-minute sit ends, simply keep going, and if you can't, two minutes is a whole sit.
Choose nothing special, no technique and no room from the depths in particular. Just sit, and let whatever the year has planted do its quiet work.

wordCard.voice: Looking back. The immeasurables, mindfulness, emptiness, koans, the elders and the diamond vehicle: a first look at depths that go much further.

orig.note: Pali gambhīra: deep; the Buddha's word for the teaching he found, deep and hard to see (MN 26).

carryVoice: Your line: there's more. Any one of those rooms is there to come back to. That closes the week.

sources.ref: Majjhima Nikaya 26 (the teaching is deep and hard to see)
Digha Nikaya 13, Tevijja Sutta (the four immeasurables)
Visuddhimagga IX (the near enemies of the immeasurables)
